key_insight: YANAMI targets multimodal conversations where each turn depends on what happened before—not just isolated prompts. It introduces a large-scale dataset and benchmark focused on stateful interaction.
problem_solved: Existing multimodal datasets largely emphasize single-turn tasks, and even multi-turn examples often allow turns to be solved independently. This leaves a gap in training and evaluating models that must maintain and update information across a conversation.
method: Introduce YANAMI as a large-scale multimodal dataset and benchmark for multiturn stateful interaction.
Focus on cross-turn dependencies requiring models to understand, maintain, and update conversational state.
Specific dataset construction procedures and evaluation metrics are not available in the provided, truncated abstract.
impact: YANAMI could help practitioners train and assess multimodal assistants that remain consistent across iterative conversations. The supplied excerpt does not include experimental results, so performance gains cannot be established.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: independent single-turn tasks versus linked, stateful conversation turns.
Conversation timeline showing visual and textual information carried forward and updated.
Unified-model hub connecting visual understanding, generation, and editing.
Memory-state cards illustrating what the model must retain after each turn.
paper_title: YANAMI: A Large-Scale Multimodal Dataset and Benchmark for Multiturn Stateful Interaction
paper_authors: Shengyu Wang, Tengyue Nong, Junming Liu, Haosong Peng, Siyu Li
